title: Protocol to segment and characterize the morphometry of individual cross-sectioned striated muscle fibers from adult murine models
protocol: Press the ctrl key while left clicking on the next fiber to be segmented.
The outline of the fixed cell turns into green.
Click on ‘Convert AOI(s) to Objects’ to convert segmented fibers to numbered objects.
Adjust the ‘magic wand’ range to a value between 10 and 30 for starting segmentation.
Adjust the ‘magic wand’ smooth to a value between 3 and 5 for post-filtering of the outline.
Left click inside the fiber to define its outline.
Slightly alter the position of the left click until the red outline fits the muscle fiber properly.
Mark the limit of muscular fibers accurately for accurate measurements.
Press ctrl and left click inside the next fiber to be analyzed when the outline is adequate.
The contour of the first selected fiber will change to green upon correct selection.
Do not keep the ctrl button pressed while adjusting the outline of the fiber.
Restart the segmentation if any fiber is incorrectly segmented due to lack of undo function.
Repeat the previous step until all fibers from the image are outlined in green.
Right click on the image when all fibers have been correctly segmented.
Click on the count/size icon to start variable acquisition.
Select measurements by clicking Measure → Select measurements.
Click on 'measure'.
Choose the measurements of interest: Area, Area/box, Aspect, Radius Ratio and Roundness.
Calculate all variables for each muscle fiber by clicking the measure button.
In the count/size window, click on File, then ‘data to clipboard’.
Select the following measurements: Area, Area/box, Aspect, Radius ratio and Roundness.
Click ok.
At the count/size window: Edit → Convert AOI(s) to object(s).
The contour of all segmented fibers will become red, and each fiber will be numbered from top to bottom.
In the count/size window: file → data to clipboard.
Paste data from the first image in an Excel spreadsheet.
Repeat steps 1–10 for all images of all participants (animals) and experimental groups.
Save this spreadsheet as ‘MusMA raw data’; create a tab to each condition to facilitate pasting your data to the spreadsheet of analysis.
In the 'Measure' menu → Snap measurements to save the image with the segmented fibers.
Download and open the ‘MusMA clear.xls’ Excel file.
In the ‘normal fibers and settings’ worksheet, paste data of at least 50 normal fibers into the yellow-marked cells starting from C11 through G11.
Set the parameters of normal (or 'regular') fibers in the ‘normal fibers and settings’ worksheet.
Define the thresholds that separate different subpopulations of muscle fibers according to their morphometry.
Set the number of standard deviations related to the average of Area and MusFII.
Adjust the thresholds to define the quadrants.
Paste raw data of all conditions in the box indicated by the blue arrow.
Alter the number of standard deviations (red cells in S column) to define the quadrants that separate subpopulations of fibers.
Paste raw data in the C13 cell for each condition, as indicated by the black arrow.
Duplicate the 'Condition 2' tab to generate as many 'condition' tabs as necessary based on the number of experimental conditions.
Generate Area x MusFII dot blot automatically.
Delete the “X” in cells where there do not contain any data.
Adjust the number of standard deviations related to the average of fibers’ area and MusFII to set the ellipse surrounding ‘normal fibers’.
Set the normal ellipse by adjusting the number of standard deviations so that it fits as many normal fibers as possible while leaving the smallest possible empty area inside.
Paste data from all experimental conditions into the light-yellow cells below ‘setting the thresholds’.
Adjust thresholds by altering the number of standard deviations in S4, S6 and S8 cells.
Duplicate the "Condition" tab to generate a tab for each condition or experimental group.
Paste raw data in the yellow box (B13 through G13 cells down) in each ‘Condition’ worksheet.
Ensure column A contains specific information for each experiment / animal / patient.
